name: Diphenhydramine
warning: Deliriant presentation is deliberately unsettling: realistic peripheral hallucinations, shadow figures, insect-like motion. One-time confirmation required.
tierNotes: Threshold: unease — slight darkening, nothing nameable.
Light: first dark specks in the corners of the frame; the faintest realistic drift on structure, barely there.

Common: skitter clusters in periphery/dark regions + smoke wisps drifting; blur waves begin; drift/jitter on edges is now visible if you look for it — the room feels subtly, unnamably wrong rather than static.
Strong: shadow faces fading in from the darkest regions, dissolving on approach; heavy blur waves; double vision begins (late curve); drift is unmistakable but stays realistic, never geometric.

Heavy: 'someone standing there' figure events, near-monochrome sickly cast, constant peripheral motion, constant double vision; a stronger, slower whole-room breathing pattern warp on top of the base drift, PLUS a genuine organic form-constant pattern riding the image's own texture (patternMask, late curve) — reuses the shared P3 pattern pass, which runs before the desaturation step, so the pattern itself arrives already muted/near-monochrome rather than colorful. User feedback wanted more psychedelic-like patterning at Heavy while staying true to the deliriant identity (no rainbow).
